answer: Each identity must complete a sequential verifiable-delay proof chained to its own key before it can act, like water forced through a single narrow delta channel: every step depends on the last, so no amount of extra hardware speeds it up. The proof is anchored to a basalt-hard registry entry that only that identity can extend, and each fake must climb its own ledge of ten minutes of unbroken sequential work, one ledge at a time, in order. A farm of a thousand fakes therefore pays a thousand sequential ten-minute ledges, while one honest identity pays only one.
